properties.rule: pix2.c:3494 (pixCleanupByteProcessing): "This must be called after processing that was initiated by pixSetupByteProcessing() has finished." The harness keeps exactly one line-pointer array (pixSetupByteProcessing allocates it, pixCleanupByteProcessing frees it), so no object identity is needed at the event level: a cleanup may only run while a setup is outstanding.
properties.formula: (!cleanup_use W setup_ok) & G(cleanup_ok -> X(!cleanup_use W setup_ok))

cleanup_use.meaning: pixCleanupByteProcessing is about to be called

cleanup_ok.meaning: pixCleanupByteProcessing freed it and closed the pairing

examples.reason: a second setup replaces the first outstanding array (utils1/pix2 pair, one live array)
the line-pointer array was already freed

properties.rule: utils1.c:1146-1154 (startTimerNested/stopTimerNested): the example shows a L_TIMER from startTimerNested being handed to stopTimerNested, which frees it; a second stop for the same timer would free it twice. The harness keeps one outstanding timer, so the pairing is event-level.
properties.formula: (!stop_use W start_ok) & G(stop_ok -> X(!stop_use W start_ok))

stop_use.meaning: stopTimerNested is about to be called

stop_ok.meaning: stopTimerNested freed it and closed the pairing

examples.reason: the timer was already freed by the first stop

unconstrainedReason: Everything else is left unconstrained on purpose. leptonica's object arguments come from typed pools with K slots per type (K = 3, 4 for PIX/PIXA/BOXA/NUMA/L_DNA/PTA/SARRAY}, and a pool slot is addressed by a payload byte, not by identity: two calls that mention PIX #2 may or may not be the same object, since a slot can be refilled (by a creator, by an out-parameter, or by the harness's default object) between them. Any rule of the form 'object X may not be used after it was destroyed' is therefore not expressible in an alphabet of call/ok events: the events do not name the object. What the library documents as a sequence rule at that level is also not a rule: leptonica overloads NULL and mismatched arguments as documented error returns (`l_ok` 0/1, or NULL), and it does not define 'use after destroy' as an error - pixDestroy() nulls the caller's pointer (pix1.c:599), so the caller cannot pass a stale object through the API at all. The one family that IS identity-free is the pair of functions whose argument is a harness-owned singleton (the byte-processing line-pointer array and the nested timer), and those are the two properties above.
